<!-- generated by docs/generate.sh - edit the super(...) of each /ctml subcommand in src/, not this file -->

The `/ctml` command, on a Paper, Spigot or Bukkit server. Every subcommand needs the `craftytml.use`
permission, which ops have, and where a player is optional it is whoever runs the command. The same lines
are what `/ctml help` prints in game, and [Paper and Spigot](/ctml/tutorial/paper) walks through using them.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`/ctml open`](#open) | Shows a registered ui to a player. |
| [`/ctml run`](#run) | Runs a script from the ui folder again, as a ui of that player's own. |
| [`/ctml execute`](#execute) | Shows ctml written into the command itself. |
| [`/ctml hologram`](#hologram) | Stands a ui in the world for everyone to see. |
| [`/ctml variable`](#variable) | Lists, sets or clears the variables of an executed ui or a hologram. |
| [`/ctml callback`](#callback) | Lists, sets or clears the callback commands of an executed ui or a hologram. |
| [`/ctml list`](#list) | Lists the registered uis and the windows open now. |
| [`/ctml demo`](#demo) | Shows the intro, and the full demo from its button. |
| [`/ctml close`](#close) | Closes a player's window. |
| [`/ctml help`](#help) | Shows these commands, or one of them in detail. |

## open

```text
/ctml open <name> [player]
```

Shows a registered ui to a player.

- name is a ui in the registry: /ctml list registered names them.
- Leave the player out to show it to yourself.

## run

```text
/ctml run <script> [player]
```

Runs a script from the ui folder again, as a ui of that player's own.

- script is a file in plugins/CraftyTML/ui.
- The script sees the player as player, and the tree it builds is not registered.

## execute

```text
/ctml execute [targets] [name] [json] <ctml>
```

Shows ctml written into the command itself.

- targets is a player or a selector like @a, and defaults to you.
- name is what variable and callback find it by, and defaults to default.
- json maps callbacks to commands run from the console: {"buy":"give {player} diamond 1"}.
- Everything after that is the ctml, built afresh for every target.

## hologram

```text
/ctml hologram create|open|demo|move|remove|list <id> [x y z] [yaw] ...
```

Stands a ui in the world for everyone to see.

- create &lt;id&gt; [x y z] [yaw] [json] &lt;ctml&gt;: ctml written into the command, with callbacks like execute's.
- open &lt;id&gt; &lt;ui&gt; [x y z] [yaw]: a registered ui.
- demo [id] [x y z] [yaw]: the intro and the demo, with all their callbacks, under the id demo unless named.
- move &lt;id&gt; [x y z] [yaw], remove &lt;id&gt;, and list.
- Coordinates take ~ like any command; without them it goes 3 blocks in front of you.
- yaw is the way its front faces; without it, it faces you.
- Anyone looking at it within 6 blocks gets a cursor and can click it; hover follows the nearest of them.
- variable and callback reach it by its id.
- Holograms are gone after a restart.

## variable

```text
/ctml variable list|put|remove [name] [variable] [value]
```

Lists, sets or clears the variables of an executed ui or a hologram.

- put &lt;name&gt; &lt;variable&gt; &lt;value&gt;: the value is the rest of the line.
- remove &lt;name&gt; &lt;variable&gt;, and list [name] for one ui or all of them.
- Every window open under the name changes straight away, and every one executed under it later.

## callback

```text
/ctml callback list|put|remove [name] [callback] [command]
```

Lists, sets or clears the callback commands of an executed ui or a hologram.

- put &lt;name&gt; &lt;callback&gt; &lt;command&gt;: {player} in the command is whoever pressed it.
- remove &lt;name&gt; &lt;callback&gt;, and list [name] for one ui or all of them.
- Only a press runs the command, never a hover.

## list

```text
/ctml list [registered|running]
```

Lists the registered uis and the windows open now.

- registered: the uis loaded from the ui folder or registered from java.
- running: every window open right now, by name, with who has it open.
- With neither, both.

## demo

```text
/ctml demo [player]
```

Shows the intro, and the full demo from its button.

- Needs intro.ctml and demo_screen.ctml in the ui folder.

## close

```text
/ctml close [player]
```

Closes a player's window.

- Leave the player out to close your own. Sneaking closes it too.

## help

```text
/ctml help [command]
```

Shows these commands, or one of them in detail.
